issue.title: Python and Rust xprompt argument scanners still disagree on quoting, escapes, and bracket nesting
issue.description:
Six xprompt/directive argument scanners implement overlapping but divergent
dialects of one grammar. Epic sase-sn unified only the `[[...]]` text-block
closing rule and the `+`-to-space decoding across them, and deliberately left
quoting, escape handling, and bracket nesting divergent (see the epic plan's
"Out of scope" section and the PROPOSED FOLLOW-UP note on sase-sn.5). The
result is that the launcher, the ACE editor, the LSP diagnostics, and the
fan-out planner can still each reach a different conclusion about the same
prompt.

Verified divergence (2026-08-24, sase master 1907346f8, sase-core-rs 0.31.11):
Rust parses a bare apostrophe in a `%clan` argument correctly; Python raises.

Single quotes: Python `_top_level_delimiter_positions` and
`_find_matching_delimiter_for_args` treat `'` as a string quote even in free
prose; the Rust `agent_launch` parsers track only backtick and `"`. An
unbalanced `'` therefore swallows every following separator on the Python side.

Backticks: `editor::directive::QuoteState` and the `agent_launch` parsers treat
`` ` `` as a quote; `editor::xprompt_args::ArgScanner` and both Python scanners
do not.

Escapes: only `alt_inspect._top_level_offsets` honors `\` escapes; no Rust
scanner does.

Bracket nesting: `find_matching_paren_for_args` and the `agent_launch` parsers
track `([{`/`)]}` depth, but `_top_level_delimiter_positions` does not, so
`#f(outer (a, b) c)` splits into two arguments while the enclosing paren match
sees one.

These are one defect, not four: each scanner's rule is only meaningful relative
to the others, and fixing any one in isolation increases divergence. The
remediation is a single shared quoting-and-nesting definition applied to all six
scanners in both repos, mirroring how sase-sn shared the text-block rule via
`find_text_block_close_for_args` (Python) and `crates/sase_core/src/xprompt_text_block.rs`
(Rust), with the shared `tests/fixtures/xprompt_args_corpus.json` extended to
cover the new cases.

This changes existing parses, so it needs a planning handoff rather than a
direct edit.

task_type_fields.impact:
## Impact

A prompt whose directive argument contains a bare apostrophe fails at launch on
the Python path with a misleading "missing closing ')'" error, while the Rust
typed-launch planner accepts it. Users writing ordinary English prose in a
`%clan` summary, an `%alt` branch, or an xprompt argument hit this. Epic sase-sn
reduced the blast radius (prose routed through a correctly delimited `[[...]]`
text block is now inert), so this is a correctness and consistency defect rather
than a frequent launch blocker.
task_type_fields.repro:
## Repro

Run from a sase workspace after `just install`:

```bash
./.venv/bin/python -c "
from sase.agent.multi_prompt_reference_directives import extract_static_clan_directive
seg = \"%clan(research.x, summary=don't stop, tribe=research)\nbody\"
print(extract_static_clan_directive(seg))
"
```

Python raises:
`DirectiveError: Malformed %clan(...) directive: missing closing ')'.`

The identical prompt parses correctly through the Rust core:

```bash
./.venv/bin/python -c "
import sase_core_rs as c
p = \"%clan(research.x, summary=don't stop, tribe=research)\nbody\"
u = c.plan_typed_launch_units(p, 'multi_prompt', 'sase')['units'][0]['payload']
print(u['clan'], u['clan_tribe'], repr(u['clan_summary']))
"
# research.x research \"don't stop\"
```

Nested-paren asymmetry, same tree:

```bash
./.venv/bin/python -c "
from sase.xprompt._parsing_args import parse_args
print(parse_args('outer (a, b) c'))   # (['outer (a', 'b) c'], {}) -- expected one argument
print(parse_args(\"it's fine, b\"))    # ([\"it's fine, b\"], {}) -- expected two arguments
"
```
